title: Inspecting What a Python Closure Captures
description: Mutate a shared nonlocal variable across two closures and inspect __code__.co_freevars and __closure__ to see what Python stores.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `make()` defines two local strings (`secret = "original"` and `hidden = "never used by the inner function"`). It returns two inner functions: `peek()` reads `secret`, and `poke(v)` uses `nonlocal secret` to update `secret = v`.
Line 11 unpacks `peek, poke = make()`. Line 13 prints `peek()` (`'original'`), line 14 calls `poke("changed")`, and line 15 calls `peek()` again.

steps.question: After `poke("changed")` runs on line 14, what does `peek()` return on line 15, and what dictionary does `dict(zip(names, cells))` print on line 20?
steps.answer: `peek()` returns `'changed'`, and line 20 prints `{'secret': 'changed'}` because `peek.__code__.co_freevars` contains `('secret',)` and its cell holds `'changed'`.

steps.description: Lines 18-20 read `peek.__code__.co_freevars` and the `cell_contents` of each cell in `peek.__closure__`, printing `{'secret': 'changed'}`.
Lines 22-32 list three follow-up experiments on `co_freevars`, `poke.__closure__`, and calling `make()` a second time.
At trace step 13 inside `poke("changed")`, line 8 updates the shared `secret` binding to `'changed'`.
